title: PRESTO: A Framework for Predicting Software System Performance from SDLC Metrics (Design and Proof-of-Concept Evaluation) — Research Compendium (Code, Synthetic Data, and Real-World Validation Adapters)
description:
Source data, code, and paper for “PRESTO: A Framework for Predicting Software System Performance from SDLC Metrics (Design and Proof-of-Concept Evaluation)” (Rangari, Mishra, Senapati; manuscript under review at MDPI Technologies). Version v2.0.0 matches the round-3 (v6) revision of the manuscript. Includes: (1) the Gaussian copula-based synthetic SDLC data generator (with the corrected calibration and the corrected add_lag_features() implementation) and its three regenerated domains (ABC Cloud Provider, XYZ Sales Force, Card Payment Processor; 170, 200, 150 releases); (2) the shared nested-cross-validation model-selection harness used for every best-model and best-feature-subset claim, plus the nested PA-RFE, moving-block bootstrap, AR/ACF diagnostics, and paired-difference bootstrap analyses; (3) adapter/pipeline scripts and small derived outputs for four independent real-world validation datasets (TravisTorrent, Mozilla Perfherder, GHALogs, SQuaD) — bulk third-party raw data is not re-hosted, each source folder documents exactly how to fetch it from its original DOI/URL; (4) the earlier ablation/robustness scripts (nested-CV hyperparameter tuning, Siegmund-style baseline, System-Availability ablation, bootstrap and target-correlation ablation, lag-shift leakage fix); (5) per-analysis evidence files documenting each reported result; (6) the figure-generation scripts; and (7) the v6 manuscript LaTeX source and Supplementary Materials.

PRESTO is evaluated as a proof of concept, not a validated prediction method. Under nested cross-validation, non-autoregressive SDLC process features reach R² = 0.108–0.620 across three synthetic domains; a target-correlation ablation shows this is largely recovery of the generator's specified structure. Across four real-world datasets, the primary validation analyses are Mozilla Perfherder's autoregressive persistence on a real production-performance signal (R² = 0.17–0.92) and SQuaD's CVE-count (R² = 0.23) and static-analysis-enriched defect-fix (R² = 0.50) results; GHALogs reaches R² = 0.113 (n = 28,443 repositories). Confidence intervals are wide throughout, and most remaining comparisons include zero. No available dataset joins eight-phase SDLC telemetry to production uptime, so each real dataset tests only a narrower proxy outcome.

See README.md in this deposit for the full directory map and reproduction steps, and real-data/README.md for exactly what raw third-party data is excluded and how to fetch it (kept out to keep this compendium small and clonable, not because it is unavailable).
